p.text: Be ___ as it may, the deadline has not moved.

key: that

fb.incorrect_default: These are frozen subjunctives: nothing inside them can be changed. 'Be that as it may' concedes and moves on. 'Suffice it to say' signals that you are cutting the detail deliberately. 'Far be it from me' disclaims before criticising. Their power is that the reader hears the move before the content; their risk is that a wrong word makes them sound learned and clumsy at once.

grammar.label: the subjunctive in formal and legal English
grammar.form: that + subject + base verb (no -s, no 'to'); if + subject + were
grammar.meaning: states what is required or supposed rather than what is

explanation.en: 'The committee requires that every member declare an interest' — 'declare', not 'declares'. The form is the bare verb whatever the subject. It survives after verbs of demanding and recommending, after adjectives of necessity ('it is essential that…'), and in fixed phrases ('be that as it may', 'come what may', 'far be it from me').
explanation.uz: 'The committee requires that every member declare an interest' — 'declare', 'declares' emas. Ega qanday bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, fe'lning asosiy shakli ishlatiladi.

grammar.positive_example: It is essential that the annex be submitted before the deadline.
grammar.negative_example: It is essential that the annex is submitted before the deadline.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida shart-istak mayli qo'shimcha bilan beriladi; ingliz tilida u fe'lning O'ZGARMASLIGI bilan ko'rinadi, shuning uchun sezilmay qoladi.

grammar.label: formulaic subjunctives and fixed concessive phrases
grammar.form: be that as it may; come what may; suffice it to say; far be it from me; God forbid
grammar.meaning: carries a whole move in a fixed form the reader recognises at once

explanation.en: These are frozen subjunctives: nothing inside them can be changed. 'Be that as it may' concedes and moves on. 'Suffice it to say' signals that you are cutting the detail deliberately. 'Far be it from me' disclaims before criticising. Their power is that the reader hears the move before the content; their risk is that a wrong word makes them sound learned and clumsy at once.
explanation.uz: Bular qotib qolgan shakllar: ichidagi hech narsani o'zgartirib bo'lmaydi. 'Be that as it may' — tan olib, davom etish; 'suffice it to say' — tafsilotni ataylab qisqartirish.

grammar.positive_example: Be that as it may, the deadline has not moved.
grammar.negative_example: Be that as it might be, the deadline has not moved.

l1_notes.uz: Qotib qolgan iboralarni so'zma-so'z tarjima qilish mumkin emas; ularni butunligicha yodlash kerak.

story.title: It is essential that it be signed

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: You have written 'the district should submit the form before March'.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Is that advice or a requirement?

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Then 'shall', not 'should'. 'Each district shall submit the form before the first of March.'

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: It sounds exact. A district that reads 'should' and misses the date has a defence, and it is your wording that gave it to them.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The next line has 'it is essential that the annex is signed'.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: 'Be signed'. After 'it is essential that', the verb takes its bare form.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Especially then. It is the one place in modern English where the verb refuses to agree, and lawyers have kept it alive.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Be that as it may, nobody in the village will notice.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Nobody in the village reads it. The lawyer who eventually does will notice, and by then you will have retired and I shall be dead.
